scope: Manual semantic review of the final 155-callable crypto benchmark table and closest-native adapters. Numerical and frozen-artifact verification is separately reproducible with audit-benchmark.py.
review: Every public callable is represented, including public constructors, streaming methods, prepared HMAC methods, and returned tagged-hasher calls. Types, constants and private implementation classes are excluded.

The table defines IC instruction counts including call overhead, cumulative allocation, median of three fresh-canister trials, setup boundaries and independent post-measurement output checks. Plugin figures are complete measured public operations, not isolated Rust kernel costs.

RIPEMD160 native mutable objects and consuming finalization are explicitly marked [M] against immutable plugin snapshots. Input prefixes and output digests match; the table does not claim equivalent state semantics.

Bech32 conversion [E] uses the exact attributed pinned private Bitcoin convertBits implementation. Both fixtures perform the same valid 32-byte padded 8-to-5 conversion; width validation and size-limit differences are disclosed.

BLAKE3 derivation [B] composes public state flags with correct context/material domain separation. Inputs remain within the native single-chunk boundary and match official vectors. Additional long-XOF workloads compose two seek blocks for contiguous bytes 13 through 112. The original package defects remain accurately disclosed.

ECDSA signing [N] uses independently prepared RFC6979 nonces in the native fixture while plugin nonce derivation is timed. Secret and digest are identical, and exact signatures match, including curve-specific low-S behavior. Variable-time native secret arithmetic and unequal API work are disclosed.

BLS G2 rows [U] time native uncompressed EIP-2537 decode and subgroup validation with compressed output, compared with compressed plugin input and coordinate recovery. Independent Python field arithmetic verifies the same points and aggregate output. Rows [P] explicitly compare trusted predecoded native arithmetic with validating plugin byte APIs; pairing returns a Boolean. Ratios are labelled as differing contracts.

Bitcoin taprootSecretKey [S] composes native tagged hashing and parity-normalized scalar arithmetic for the same empty-tree BIP341 tweak; exact output is verified and variable-time arithmetic disclosed.

Bitcoin TaprootHasher.signatureHash [C] measures the first cold plugin call versus native uncached one-shot hashing on the same ten-input transaction. Construction is excluded, lazy common hashes are included, and native array-to-Blob oracle conversion outside timing is disclosed.

Earlier Bitcoin script/BIP32 validation gaps were corrected in the selected validated native stage. Final measurement selection pins the corrected fixture source and independent output, preventing reuse of the earlier fixtures.

All 12 hash/codec, two ECDSA and two Bitcoin closest-adapter cases subsequently completed three actual native trials with unchanged matching plugin oracles. This resolves the pending runtime note in the earlier static hash/codec child report.

All 140 displayed native comparisons represent the same mathematical workload, with material preparation, representation, validation and mutability differences stated in table markers or per-row evidence. Additional sizes remain available in the 181-row machine-readable evidence.

BIP340 Schnorr.reason: Pinned native packages do not implement this signature scheme; ECDSA is not a mathematical counterpart.

BIP143.reason: Pinned Bitcoin package has no BIP143 message construction or prepared hasher.

Retained Taproot construction.reason: Native one-shot Taproot hashing exists and is compared for digest operations, but no retained common-hash-state constructor exists.

RFC9380 and BLS signature profiles.reason: Pinned package provides curve mapping and arithmetic, but not the complete required RFC9380 XMD hash-to-curve and profile-specific signature operations. Mapping and pairing alone perform different work.

closed_review_issues: Explicit final plugin stage and current source/artifact fingerprints prevent mixing historical optimized builds.
Closest available native BLS arithmetic, RIPEMD state operations, ECDSA signing, Bech32 conversion, BLAKE3 composition and Bitcoin operations replace avoidable blank cells.
BLS workload names and sizes are concrete; Base58 decode size correctly states 111 input characters and 82 output bytes.
Stale prose claiming unavailable native BLAKE3 derivation/long-XOF is replaced by accurate bounded-composition notes.
Native validation differences in Bitcoin fixtures are corrected or visibly disclosed, with fresh selected measurements.
limitations: Closest-operation ratios with markers are not equivalent-contract or side-channel speedup guarantees.
Review covers the recorded valid workloads and retained malformed-input audit suites; it does not establish formal cryptographic correctness or constant-time behavior.
Missing peers are assessed against the pinned packages, not every possible unpublished or future native implementation.
